---
title: Quickstart
description: Add uploads, webhooks and private playback to a Next.js app in four steps.
icon: Rocket
---

By the end of this page, a signed-in user of your app uploads a video from the
browser, your database hears when it's ready, and a viewer your app allows
watches it, encrypted. The browser never sees a ClipMux key.

It takes one command, one route file, two elements and three callbacks. The
same handler runs in [Express](/docs/build/frameworks/express),
[Hono](/docs/build/frameworks/hono) and
[other Fetch runtimes](/docs/build/frameworks/fetch-runtimes).

## Before you start

- A ClipMux server, for example `https://video.example.com`, and an owner
  account on it to approve your app. To run one, see
  [Install with one line](/docs/self-host/install).
- A Next.js app with the App Router, on Node 20.19 or later.

## Add ClipMux

<Steps>
<Step>

### Connect the app

<Tabs items={['npm', 'pnpm']}>
<Tab value="npm">

```bash
npm i @clipmux/node @clipmux/uploader @clipmux/player
npx @clipmux/node init --server https://video.example.com
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="pnpm">

```bash
pnpm add @clipmux/node @clipmux/uploader @clipmux/player
pnpm dlx @clipmux/node init --server https://video.example.com
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

`init` opens an approval page on your ClipMux server. Approve the app there,
as the owner, and `init` writes its credentials to `.env.local`:
`CLIPMUX_URL`, `CLIPMUX_API_KEY`, `CLIPMUX_SIGNING_KID`,
`CLIPMUX_SIGNING_KEY` and `CLIPMUX_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. It never prints them.
Keep `.env.local` out of git.

</Step>
<Step>

### Add one route file

<include cwd lang="ts" meta='title="app/api/clipmux/[action]/route.ts"'>snippets/node/nextjs/route.ts</include>

The file answers POST requests on three of your app's routes: `/api/clipmux/upload`, `/playback` and
`/webhook`. `requireInstructor`, `getUser`, `canWatch` and `db` stand for
your own code. Every route refuses by default: a callback you leave out is a
404, and one that returns `null` is a 403.

`passthrough` is your own ID for the video. It comes back on every webhook,
so you can find the record it belongs to. See
[Link videos to your records](/docs/build/upload/passthrough).

</Step>
<Step>

### Add two elements

<include cwd lang="tsx" meta='title="app/lessons/[id]/video.tsx"'>snippets/node/nextjs/video.tsx</include>

The uploader sends the file in parts straight to storage, and resumes if the
connection drops. The player asks your `playback` callback for a token before
it plays, and again when the token runs out. Outside React, the same two
elements work in plain HTML:

```html
<script type="module">
  import '@clipmux/uploader/element'
  import '@clipmux/player/element'
</script>
<clipmux-uploader create-url="/api/clipmux/upload?lesson=42"></clipmux-uploader>
<clipmux-player playback-id="pid_…" session-url="/api/clipmux/playback"></clipmux-player>
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Check it

```bash
npx @clipmux/node doctor
```

`doctor` checks every credential and ends with `✓ Ready.` It also prints the
origins your Content-Security-Policy must allow.

While you develop, your laptop can't receive webhooks from the server, so
forward them:

```bash
npx @clipmux/node listen --forward-to localhost:3000/api/clipmux/webhook
```

</Step>
</Steps>

## Check it works

1. Open a lesson page, choose a short video in the uploader and wait for it
   to finish.
2. Watch the `listen` terminal: `video.asset.ready` arrives when encoding is
   done, and your `asset` callback stores the status and the playback ID.
3. Reload the page. The video plays.

To test without the browser, upload a file from the terminal:

```bash
npx @clipmux/node upload sample.mp4 --passthrough lesson_42 --wait
```

If a step fails, [Troubleshooting](/docs/build/going-live/troubleshooting)
lists each error and what to do.
